                                                                                 1 UC Regs, reg 66(1)(b)(iii)


Note 1: The Scottish carer’s allowance supplement1, paid by the Scottish Government to those recipients
of CA living in Scotland, is not the same as CA and is fully disregarded.


                                                                               The Scotland Act 2018, s47


Note 2: The Scottish Government has awarded an additional payment of £230.10 in respect of the

period 01.04.20 to 30.09.201. These payments are fully disregarded.

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"78058 [see DMG memo 02/25] DMs should normally treat an award of CA/UC that includes the carer
element as a proper award until the CA/UC that includes the carer element decision is revised,
superseded or otherwise changed on appeal. If the claimant says that


1. they are not being cared for by the person getting CA/UC that includes the carer element or


2. the award of CA/UC that includes the carer element is in error or


3. they know nothing about the CA/UC that includes the carer element award or


4. the CA/UC that includes the carer element claim is fraudulent


the DM should ask the CA unit or the office responsible for the UC award to investigate whether the CA
or the UC that includes the carer element award is correctly made.

28050 When calculating income other than earnings for IS and JSA(IB) 1 DMs should take

2. BA


3. CA


4. CHB


5. cash in lieu of concessionary coal


6. CTC


7. ESA(Cont)


8. Ministry of Justice ex gratia incapacity allowances (previously paid by the Home Office)


9. IB


10. IIDB


11. JSA(Cont)


12. MA


13. personal pensions


14. PB and MDB scheme


15. refund of income tax


16. RP


17. SDA


18. SP


19. War orphan's pension


20. WTC


21. WP

22. WC


fully into account. These are most common types of income that DMs deal with although there are other
types too. Detailed guidance is given in DMG 28052 et seq.
